newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids hold despite crude, USG still firm.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids hold despite crude, USG still firm.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Wednesday in lackluster trade, with the Gulf Coast still fairly well supported by demand into Florida and recent high sulphur interest for Mexico, sources said.

"We've had some good heat in Florida, but the East may be prone to some weakness," said one cash trader, noting the crude selloff had little impact on resid but softer East Coast gas prices recently made that fuel more competitive.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent held firmely in the low-$16 a barrel area, helped by forecasts for more heat in Florida and reports of a utility tender, traders said.
A Florida utility tendered for 180,000 barrels of one percent for August 5 delivery. Bids are due Thursday.

USG three percent again gained slightly to the low-$14s on reports of a fairly prompt 150,000 barrel deal at $14.35 (FOB Houston). The high sulphur market also was supported by recent buying interest for Mexico.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was steady to down slightly at $16.80-17.05.
New York high sulphurs again were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still talked in the low-$15s.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was flat at $18.00-25.

New York city gate swing gas prices were unchanged again Wednesday in the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $15.00 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, moved up by two to three cents to about $2.16/mmBtu, or $13.61 a barrel.
